findings.title: Backup code verification/consumption is not atomic, allowing reuse
findings.body: In the credentials authorize() callback, the backup code is read from `user.backupCodes`, checked for a match, and only afterwards persisted back with the matched code nulled out (lines 131-156). There is no transaction or row lock between the read and the write. If two concurrent login attempts submit the same backup code before either update completes, both requests will see the code as still valid and both will succeed, effectively allowing a single-use backup code to be used more than once. This defeats the 'exactly once' guarantee stated in the backup_code_instructions translation string.

findings.title: Explicit type="password" prop breaks the password visibility toggle
findings.body: The password field was switched from a plain TextField to the PasswordField component, but an explicit `type="password"` prop is still passed (line 176). PasswordField (packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx) computes `type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"}` and then spreads `{...props}` afterward, so any caller-supplied `type` prop overrides the computed value. Because `type="password"` is passed here, clicking the show/hide-password eye icon in this dialog will never reveal the password, unlike other usages of PasswordField (e.g. in DisableTwoFactorModal) that don't pass a type prop.

findings.title: Backup code login unavailable for identity-provider (SSO) 2FA flow
findings.body: When `totpEmail` is set (the identity-provider/SAML/Google 2FA redirect flow), the footer renders `ExternalTotpFooter` instead of `TwoFactorFooter` (line ~182). `ExternalTotpFooter` has no 'Lost access' control, so `twoFactorLostAccess` can never be toggled to true for these users, and the BackupCode component is effectively unreachable even though it's referenced in the render logic. Users who signed up via Google/SAML, enabled 2FA, and then lose access to their authenticator have no way to use a backup code to regain access through this login path, unlike regular CAL-identity users.

findings.title: No test coverage for logging in with a backup code
findings.body: The PR adds backup-code-based login as a core part of the feature (per the PR description and demo video), but the only e2e coverage added exercises the backup codes display/download/copy UI during setup, not the actual login-with-backup-code flow or disabling 2FA via a backup code. The added comment '// TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup' explicitly acknowledges this gap. Given this is a security-sensitive account-recovery mechanism, lacking a test that verifies a backup code can actually authenticate a user (and that it is single-use) is a significant gap.

findings.title: Used backup codes are nulled rather than removed, leaving stale entries
findings.body: After a successful backup code login, `backupCodes[index] = null` is used to invalidate the used code instead of filtering it out of the array (line 148). Over repeated logins the encrypted backupCodes JSON blob accumulates null placeholders indefinitely instead of shrinking, which is unnecessary data bloat and makes it harder to reason about how many valid codes remain without decrypting and counting non-null entries.

findings.title: Backup codes download Blob URL is never revoked on modal close/cancel
findings.body: `URL.createObjectURL(textBlob)` is called in handleSetup (line 99) and only revoked the next time `handleSetup` runs again (line 98: `if (backupCodesUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl);`). If the user cancels the dialog or closes it via the 'close'/'enable' flow without starting a new 2FA setup, the object URL is never revoked, leaking the Blob for the lifetime of the page.
